  "old_string": "\\paragraph{Comparison with KIVI.}\nKIVI~\\cite{liu2024kivi} uses asymmetric per-channel quantization with per-token scaling---a finer-grained quantization \\emph{scheme} than our symmetric per-channel approach, applied uniformly across all heads.\nAt 4-bit with no residual channels ($r{=}0$), KIVI achieves 9.91 PPL on Qwen2.5-7B (vs.\\ 9.81 bf16) and 8.14 on Llama-3.1-8B (vs.\\ 8.09), both near-lossless; our symmetric uniform 4-bit yields 15.45 and 8.47, respectively.\nThe gap reflects the quantization scheme, not allocation strategy.\nHowever, KIVI cannot exploit head-level heterogeneity: on Qwen (spread pattern), constrained MCKP reduces our symmetric 4-bit from 15.45 to 10.91, a $-$4.54 PPL improvement from reallocating bits across heads---a degree of freedom unavailable to any uniform-precision method.\nOn Llama (spike), the allocation gain is negligible ($-$0.02), consistent with the heterogeneity analysis.\nAt 2-bit ($r{=}0$), KIVI degrades to 13.34 on Qwen and 10.08 on Llama, as all heads---including the most sensitive---receive the same precision.\nThe two approaches are orthogonal: KIVI determines \\emph{how} to quantize each head (asymmetric scaling), while our method determines \\emph{at what precision} (bit-width selection across heads).\nComposing KIVI's per-channel scheme with per-head mixed-precision allocation is a natural extension.",
  "new_string": "\\paragraph{Comparison with KIVI.}\nKIVI~\\cite{liu2024kivi} uses asymmetric per-channel quantization with per-token scaling, applied uniformly across all heads.\nAt 4-bit ($r{=}0$), KIVI achieves near-lossless PPL (9.91 on Qwen, 8.14 on Llama vs.\\ 9.81/8.09 bf16), while our symmetric scheme yields 15.45 and 8.47---a gap from the quantization method, not allocation.\nHowever, KIVI cannot exploit head-level heterogeneity: on Qwen (spread), constrained MCKP reduces symmetric 4-bit from 15.45 to 10.91 ($-$4.54 PPL) by reallocating bits across heads, a degree of freedom unavailable to uniform-precision methods; on Llama (spike), the gain is negligible ($-$0.02).\nAt 2-bit ($r{=}0$), KIVI degrades to 13.34 on Qwen and 10.08 on Llama, as all heads---including sensitive ones---receive the same precision.\nThe two approaches are orthogonal---KIVI selects the per-channel quantization scheme, our method selects the per-head bit-width---and can be composed."

    "originalFile": "\\section{Experiments}\n\\label{sec:experiments}\n\n\\subsection{Experimental Setup}\n\\label{sec:setup}\n\n\\paragraph{Models.}\nWe evaluate seven models spanning five architecture families and diverse attention configurations:\n\\textbf{Qwen2.5-7B} (GQA 7:1, 28 layers $\\times$ 4 KV heads = 112),\n\\textbf{Qwen2.5-14B} (GQA 5:1, 48 $\\times$ 8 = 384),\n\\textbf{Yi-1.5-9B} (GQA 8:1, 48 $\\times$ 4 = 192),\n\\textbf{Llama-3.1-8B} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\\times$ 8 = 256),\n\\textbf{Mistral-7B-v0.3} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\\times$ 8 = 256, sliding window attention),\n\\textbf{Gemma-2-9B} (GQA 2:1, 42 $\\times$ 8 = 336, \\texttt{head\\_dim}=256, attention logit softcapping),\nand \\textbf{Pythia-1.4B} (MHA 1:1, 24 $\\times$ 16 = 384).\nThis selection spans GQA ratios from 1:1 (MHA) to 8:1 and covers standard, sliding-window, softcapped, and multi-head attention.\n\n\\paragraph{Evaluation.}\nWe report perplexity (PPL, $\\downarrow$) on the WikiText-2 test split (298{,}938 tokens) under bf16 inference with stride 512.\nFor downstream evaluation, we use ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, and WinoGrande under 0-shot prompting.\n\n\\paragraph{Profiling.}\nPer-head sensitivity is measured by independently quantizing each head to each candidate bit-width in $\\{2, 4, 8, 16\\}$ and recording the PPL increase over the bf16 baseline.\nAll results use high-resolution profiling (64 sequences $\\times$ 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train); Qwen-14B and Pythia $k$ values pending).\n\n\\paragraph{Baselines.}\nWe compare against:\n(1)~uniform 4-bit quantization;\n(2)~unconstrained greedy allocation (RateQuant-style~\\cite{zuo2026ratequant});\n(3)~unconstrained MCKP allocation;\n(4)~an L0-random heuristic that assigns Layer-0 heads to 8-bit and $k$ random non-Layer-0 heads to 2-bit, with remaining heads at 4-bit (5 seeds; 78	The constraint reduces 2-bit heads from 106 to 8, confirming that it universally prevents over-allocation regardless of distribution shape.
79	
80	Unconstrained failure severity forms a three-tier gradient that tracks heterogeneity shape: \emph{catastrophic} on spread-pattern Qwen ($3.3\times$ bf16), \emph{moderate} on flat-pattern Gemma-2 ($1.47\times$, driven by 31.5\% 2-bit over-allocation), and \emph{mild} on the remaining spike/flat models (${\sim}1.07$--$1.08\times$).
81	Greedy and MCKP produce identical unconstrained allocations on 4 of 5 models; the exception is Qwen, where MCKP assigns 7 more heads to 2-bit than greedy (75 vs.\ 68), worsening its already-catastrophic PPL.
82	The allocation visualization (Figure~\ref{fig:allocation}, Appendix~\ref{sec:allocation_appendix}) and budget sweep (Appendix~\ref{sec:budget_sweep}) provide additional detail.
83	
84	MCKP consistently outperforms random L0-constrained allocation and naive positional baselines across all three tested models (median gap 5--16\%; Table~\ref{tab:heuristic} in Appendix~\ref{sec:heuristic_appendix}).
85	
86	\paragraph{Comparison with KIVI.}
87	KIVI~\cite{liu2024kivi} uses asymmetric per-channel quantization with per-token scaling, applied uniformly across all heads.
88	At 4-bit ($r{=}0$), KIVI achieves near-lossless PPL (9.91 on Qwen, 8.14 on Llama vs.\ 9.81/8.09 bf16), while our symmetric scheme yields 15.45 and 8.47---a gap from the quantization method, not allocation.
89	However, KIVI cannot exploit head-level heterogeneity: on Qwen (spread), constrained MCKP reduces symmetric 4-bit from 15.45 to 10.91 ($-$4.54 PPL) by reallocating bits across heads, a degree of freedom unavailable to uniform-precision methods; on Llama (spike), the gain is negligible ($-$0.02).
90	At 2-bit ($r{=}0$), KIVI degrades to 13.34 on Qwen and 10.08 on Llama, as all heads---including sensitive ones---receive the same precision.
91	The two approaches are orthogonal---KIVI selects the per-channel quantization scheme, our method selects the per-head bit-width---and can be composed.
92	
93	\subsection{Downstream Evaluation}
94	\label{sec:downstream}
95	
96	\begin{table}[t]
97	\centering

    "originalFile": "\\section{Experiments}\n\\label{sec:experiments}\n\n\\subsection{Experimental Setup}\n\\label{sec:setup}\n\n\\paragraph{Models.}\nWe evaluate seven models spanning five architecture families and diverse attention configurations:\n\\textbf{Qwen2.5-7B} (GQA 7:1, 28 layers $\\times$ 4 KV heads = 112),\n\\textbf{Qwen2.5-14B} (GQA 5:1, 48 $\\times$ 8 = 384),\n\\textbf{Yi-1.5-9B} (GQA 8:1, 48 $\\times$ 4 = 192),\n\\textbf{Llama-3.1-8B} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\\times$ 8 = 256),\n\\textbf{Mistral-7B-v0.3} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\\times$ 8 = 256, sliding window attention),\n\\textbf{Gemma-2-9B} (GQA 2:1, 42 $\\times$ 8 = 336, \\texttt{head\\_dim}=256, attention logit softcapping),\nand \\textbf{Pythia-1.4B} (MHA 1:1, 24 $\\times$ 16 = 384).\nThis selection spans GQA ratios from 1:1 (MHA) to 8:1 and covers standard, sliding-window, softcapped, and multi-head attention.\n\n\\paragraph{Evaluation.}\nWe report perplexity (PPL, $\\downarrow$) on the WikiText-2 test split (298{,}938 tokens) under bf16 inference with stride 512.\nFor downstream evaluation, we use ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, and WinoGrande under 0-shot prompting.\n\n\\paragraph{Profiling.}\nPer-head sensitivity is measured by independently quantizing each head to each candidate bit-width in $\\{2, 4, 8, 16\\}$ and recording the PPL increase over the bf16 baseline.\nAll results use high-resolution profiling (64 sequences $\\times$ 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train);     "originalFile": "\\section{Experiments}\n\\label{sec:experiments}\n\n\\subsection{Experimental Setup}\n\\label{sec:setup}\n\n\\paragraph{Models.}\nWe evaluate seven models spanning five architecture families and diverse attention configurations:\n\\textbf{Qwen2.5-7B} (GQA 7:1, 28 layers $\\times$ 4 KV heads = 112),\n\\textbf{Qwen2.5-14B} (GQA 5:1, 48 $\\times$ 8 = 384),\n\\textbf{Yi-1.5-9B} (GQA 8:1, 48 $\\times$ 4 = 192),\n\\textbf{Llama-3.1-8B} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\\times$ 8 = 256),\n\\textbf{Mistral-7B-v0.3} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\\times$ 8 = 256, sliding window attention),\n\\textbf{Gemma-2-9B} (GQA 2:1, 42 $\\times$ 8 = 336, \\texttt{head\\_dim}=256, attention logit softcapping),\nand \\textbf{Pythia-1.4B} (MHA 1:1, 24 $\\times$ 16 = 384).\nThis selection spans GQA ratios from 1:1 (MHA) to 8:1 and covers standard, sliding-window, softcapped, and multi-head attention.\n\n\\paragraph{Evaluation.}\nWe report perplexity (PPL, $\\downarrow$) on the WikiText-2 test split (298{,}938 tokens) under bf16 inference with stride 512.\nFor downstream evaluation, we use ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, and WinoGrande under 0-shot prompting.\n\n\\paragraph{Profiling.}\nPer-head sensitivity is measured by independently quantizing each head to each candidate bit-width in $\\{2, 4, 8, 16\\}$ and recording the PPL increase over the bf16 baseline.\nAll results use high-resolution profiling (64 sequences $\\times$ 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train); Appendix~\\ref{sec:profiling_resolution} compares against standard-resolution profiling (16 seq $\\times$ 512 tok).\n\n\\paragraph{Compression and constraint.}\nThe default target is 4$\\times$ compression (average 4 bits, budget ratio 0.25).\nThe cardinality constraint limits 2-bit assignments to at most $k$ heads, where $k$ is selected via the compounding sweep described in \\S\\ref{sec:method} ($k{=}8$ for Qwen-7B, $k{=}2$ for Yi-1.5 and Llama, $k{=}4$ for Mistral, $k{=}8$ for Gemma-2; Qwen-14B and Pythia $k$ values pending).\n\n\\paragraph{Baselines.}\nWe compare against:\n(1)~uniform 4-bit quantization;\n(2)~unconstrained greedy allocation (RateQuant-style~\\cite{zuo2026ratequant});\n(3)~unconstrained MCKP allocation;\n(4)~an L0-random heuristic that assigns Layer-0 heads to 8-bit and $k$ random non-Layer-0 heads to 2-bit, with remaining heads at 4-bit (5 seeds; we report mean$\\pm$std and median);\nand (5)~a naive positional heuristic that assigns Layer-0 to 8-bit and the $k$ deepest heads to 2-bit.\n\n\\subsection{Main Results}\n\\label{sec:main_results}\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{PPL ($\\downarrow$) on WikiText-2 at 4$\\times$ compression. Unconstrained failure severity forms a three-tier gradient: \\emph{catastrophic} on Qwen-7B ($3.3\\times$ bf16), \\emph{moderate} on Gemma-2 ($1.5\\times$), \\emph{mild} on the remaining models (${\\sim}1.1\\times$). Greedy and MCKP produce identical unconstrained allocations on 4/5 models. Best constrained result per model in \\textbf{bold}; --- = experiment pending. $^\\ddagger$Best $k$ from ablation ($k{=}4$). $^*$BOS-corrected.}\n\\label{tab:main_results}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccc}\n\\toprule\nModel & Baseline & Uniform & \\multicolumn{2}{c}{Unconstrained} & Ours \\\\\n\\cmidrule(lr){4-5}\n & (bf16) & (4-bit) & Greedy & MCKP & (Constr.) \\\\\n\\midrule\nQwen2.5-7B      & 9.81  & 15.45 & 32.45 & 36.92 & \\textbf{10.91} \\\\\nQwen2.5-14B     & 5.84  & ---   & ---   & ---   & --- \\\\\nYi-1.5-9B       & 7.02  & 7.22  & 7.56  & 7.56  & 7.22 \\\\\nLlama-3.1-8B    & 8.09  & 8.47  & 8.63  & 8.63  & \\textbf{8.45} \\\\\nMistral-7B-v0.3 & 7.04  & 7.13  & 7.57  & 7.60  & 7.16$^\\ddagger$ \\\\\nGemma-2-9B$^*$  & 6.03  & 6.17  & 8.85  & 8.85  & 6.20 \\\\\nPythia-1.4B     & 13.63 & ---   & ---   & ---   & --- \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nOn Qwen2.5-7B, constrained MCKP achieves 10.91 PPL, a 29.4\\% reduction over uniform 4-bit (15.45).\nWithout the constraint, both greedy (32.45) and MCKP (36.92) perform \\emph{worse} than uniform---a catastrophic failure from excessive 2-bit assignments compounding across layers.\nAcross 3 calibration seeds, constrained MCKP yields mean PPL 10.99$\\pm$0.06 with 90.2\\% three-way allocation agreement, confirming profiling stability.\n\nOn Llama-3.1-8B, the result is essentially indistinguishable from uniform (8.45 vs.\\ 8.47, $\\Delta < 0.02$ PPL).\nHires profiling reveals a spike pattern (concentration 0.34, $t_1/t_5{=}0.71$) dominated by a single top head (L2H5), leaving little cross-bitwidth gradient for non-uniform allocation to exploit.\n\nOn Mistral-7B-v0.3, constrained MCKP (7.16, $k{=}4$) is slightly worse than uniform (7.13, $+$0.4\\%)---a genuine negative result, as the profiler reports near-zero sensitivity differences across heads.\nMistral's sliding-window attention may contribute to this uniformity.\n\nOn Yi-1.5-9B, constrained MCKP ($k{=}2$) matches uniform at 7.22 PPL.\nDespite the highest concentration tested (0.71), sensitivity is dominated by a single outlier (L4H3, $t_1/t_5{=}0.90$), a spike pattern with no cross-bitwidth gradient to exploit.\n\nOn Gemma-2-9B$^*$ (GQA 2:1), constrained MCKP ($k{=}8$) achieves 6.20 PPL vs.\\ uniform 6.17, slightly above ($+$0.4\\%).\nDespite its flat sensitivity distribution (concentration 0.23), unconstrained MCKP degrades to 8.85 ($1.47\\times$ bf16)---a moderate failure driven by the solver assigning 31.5\\% of heads to 2-bit (vs.\\ 4.7--16.4\\% in other non-spread models).\nThe constraint reduces 2-bit heads from 106 to 8, confirming that it universally prevents over-allocation regardless of distribution shape.\n\nUnconstrained failure severity forms a three-tier gradient that tracks heterogeneity shape: \\emph{catastrophic} on spread-pattern Qwen ($3.3\\times$ bf16), \\emph{moderate} on flat-pattern Gemma-2 ($1.47\\times$, driven by 31.5\\% 2-bit over-allocation), and \\emph{mild} on the remaining spike/flat models (${\\sim}1.07$--$1.08\\times$).\nSee Appendix~\\ref{sec:allocation_appendix} (allocation visualization) and Appendix~\\ref{sec:budget_sweep} (budget sweep) for additional detail.\n\nMCKP consistently outperforms random L0-constrained allocation and naive positional baselines across all three tested models (median gap 5--16\\%; Table~\\ref{tab:heuristic} in Appendix~\\ref{sec:heuristic_appendix}).\n\n\\paragraph{Comparison with KIVI.}\nKIVI~\\cite{liu2024kivi} uses asymmetric per-channel quantization with per-token scaling, applied uniformly across all heads.\nAt 4-bit ($r{=}0$), KIVI achieves near-lossless PPL (9.91 on Qwen, 8.14 on Llama vs.\\ 9.81/8.09 bf16), while our symmetric scheme yields 15.45 and 8.47---a gap from the quantization method, not allocation.\nHowever, KIVI cannot exploit head-level heterogeneity: on Qwen (spread), constrained MCKP reduces symmetric 4-bit from 15.45 to 10.91 ($-$4.54 PPL) by reallocating bits across heads, a degree of freedom unavailable to uniform-precision methods; on Llama (spike), the gain is negligible ($-$0.02).\nAt 2-bit ($r{=}0$), KIVI degrades to 13.34 on Qwen and 10.08 on Llama, as all heads---including sensitive ones---receive the same precision.\nThe two approaches are orthogonal---KIVI selects the per-channel quantization scheme, our method selects the per-head bit-width---and can be composed.\n\n\\subsection{Downstream Evaluation}\n\\label{sec:downstream}\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{0-shot accuracy change (Ours $-$ Uniform, pts) at 4$\\times$ compression. Qwen shows large gains; the remaining models show small degradations or neutrality, tracking PPL results.}\n\\label{tab:downstream}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccc}\n\\toprule\nModel & ARC-C & HS & PIQA & WG & Avg \\\\\n\\midrule\nQwen2.5-7B        & $+$3.2 & $+$4.0 & $+$1.3 & $+$2.0 & $+$2.6 \\\\\nYi-1.5-9B        & $-$3.2 & $-$0.6 & $-$0.3 & $+$1.3 & $-$0.8 \\\\\nLlama-3.1-8B     & $-$2.7 & $-$0.1 & $-$0.7 & $-$0.2 & $-$1.0 \\\\\nMistral-7B       & $-$1.2 & $-$0.2 & $+$0.4 & $-$1.0 & $-$0.5 \\\\\nGemma-2-9B       & $-$0.2 & $+$0.3 & $-$0.1 & $+$0.8 & $+$0.1 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nOn Qwen, constrained MCKP improves average 0-shot accuracy by 2.6 pts over uniform (0.686 vs.\\ 0.660), recovering $\\sim$73\\% of the accuracy lost to quantization.\nThe four non-spread architectures show minor average degradation (Yi $-$0.8, Llama $-$1.0, Mistral $-$0.5, Gemma-2 $+$0.1 pts); Llama is the most systematic, with 0 of 5 tasks showing positive change.\nARC-Challenge shows the largest per-task sensitivity across all models (Yi $-$3.2, Llama $-$2.7, Mistral $-$1.2, Gemma-2 $-$0.2 pts), consistent with multi-step reasoning where KV cache errors accumulate across longer inference chains.\nCross-dataset stability analysis (Appendix~\\ref{sec:cross_dataset}) confirms ${>}96\\%$ bit-assignment agreement between WikiText-2 and C4 calibration across all three tested models.",
